+\subsection{Realizable collision and certificate lower bounds}
+\label{sec:realizable-collision-lower-bounds}
+
+We begin with a relative realization fact for sign determinants.  It is
+sufficient for both the explicit collision family and the abstract
+certificate-degree family.
+
+\begin{lemma}[Relative sign-determinant realization]
+\label{lem:relative-sign-determinant-realization}
+Let \(P_0,P_1\in\ZZ[z]\) satisfy
+\[
+ P_0(0)=P_1(0)=1,\qquad P_0\equiv P_1\pmod2.
+\]
+Put \(d=\max\{1,\deg P_0,\deg P_1\}\).  There are a positive integral
+\(d\times d\) matrix \(A\) and two one-step \(C_2\)-cocycles on the same
+marked base graph with sign blocks \(C_0,C_1\) such that
+\[
+ \det(I-zC_i)=P_i(z)\qquad(i=0,1),
+\]
+and both sign blocks have strict twisted spectral gap:
+\[
+ \rad(C_i)<\rad(A)\qquad(i=0,1).
+\]
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Pad both polynomials to degree \(d\), and let \(C_i\) be the integral
+companion matrix of the monic polynomial
+\[
+ t^dP_i(t^{-1}).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ \det(I-zC_i)=z^d\det(z^{-1}I-C_i)=P_i(z).
+\]
+The congruence of the polynomials makes the two standard companion matrices
+entrywise congruent modulo two.  For each entry choose a positive integer
+\(A_{jk}\), in this common parity class, with
+\[
+ A_{jk}>\max\{\abs{(C_0)_{jk}},\abs{(C_1)_{jk}}\}.
+\]
+Thus \(A\) is positive and hence primitive.  For each \(i\), the non-negative
+integral matrices
+\[
+ \frac{A+C_i}{2},\qquad \frac{A-C_i}{2}
+\]
+count respectively the \(e\)- and \(s\)-labelled edges of a \(C_2\)-cocycle
+on this same marked base.  Finally,
+\[
+ \rad(C_i)\le\rad(\abs{C_i})<\rad(A)
+\]
+by strict Perron--Frobenius monotonicity, proving the gap.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{theorem}[Realizable linear multi-collisions]
+\label{thm:realizable-linear-multicollisions}
+For every integer \(m\ge1\), there is a positive primitive directed
+multigraph with
+\[
+ v_m=4m+2
+\]
+vertices and two one-step \(C_2\)-cocycles \(\tau_m,\tau_m'\) on the same
+marked base, both with strict twisted spectral gap, for which the primitive
+length--element data differ but
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:realizable-linear-profile-collisions}
+ \mathcal E_e^{\tau_m}(y_{m,i})
+ =\mathcal E_e^{\tau_m'}(y_{m,i}),\qquad
+ \mathcal E_s^{\tau_m}(y_{m,i})
+ =\mathcal E_s^{\tau_m'}(y_{m,i})
+ \quad(1\le i\le m)
+\end{equation}
+at \(m\) distinct rational radii in the open Perron interval.
+
+More explicitly, put
+\[
+ s_i=64(m+1)+4i\qquad(1\le i\le m)
+\]
+and let \(C_m\) be the \((2m+1)\times(2m+1)\) integral matrix indexed by
+\[
+ u_0,\ldots,u_m,w_1,\ldots,w_m
+\]
+whose only non-zero entries are
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:realizable-collision-Cm-entries}
+ \begin{aligned}
+  (C_m)_{u_{i-1},u_i}&=-4,&
+  (C_m)_{u_{i-1},w_i}&=s_i &&(1\le i\le m),\\
+  (C_m)_{w_i,u_i}&=s_i,&
+  (C_m)_{u_m,u_0}&=-4.
+ \end{aligned}
+\end{equation}
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:realizable-collision-Qm}
+ Q_m(z):=\det(I-zC_m)
+ =1+4z\prod_{i=1}^m(-4z+s_i^2z^2).
+\end{equation}
+Writing \(n=2m+1\), take the two \(2n\times2n\) sign blocks
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:realizable-collision-sign-blocks}
+ B_m=\begin{pmatrix}0&C_m/2\\2I_n&0\end{pmatrix},
+ \qquad B_m'=C_m\oplus C_m.
+\end{equation}
+They satisfy
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:realizable-collision-determinants}
+ \det(I-zB_m)=Q_m(z^2),\qquad
+ \det(I-zB_m')=Q_m(z)^2.
+\end{equation}
+The common base may be chosen as
+\[
+ A_m=s_mJ_{4m+2},\qquad
+ \lambda_m=s_m(4m+2),
+\]
+and the collision radii are
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:realizable-collision-radii}
+ y_{m,i}=\frac4{s_i^2}\qquad(1\le i\le m).
+\end{equation}
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+In the directed support of \(C_m\), every non-trivial cycle must traverse
+from \(u_0\) through the stages \(1,\ldots,m\) and then use the closing edge
+\(u_m\to u_0\).  At stage \(i\), it uses either the direct edge of weight
+\(-4\), contributing \(-4z\), or the two-edge detour through \(w_i\),
+contributing \(s_i^2z^2\).  A single directed cycle contributes the negative
+of the product of its weighted \(z\)-edges to \(\det(I-zC_m)\).  The closing
+edge contributes \(-4z\), so summing the \(2^m\) choices gives
+\[
+ 1-(-4z)\prod_{i=1}^m(-4z+s_i^2z^2),
+\]
+which is \eqref{eq:realizable-collision-Qm}.
+
+All entries of \(C_m\) are divisible by four.  Hence the blocks in
+\eqref{eq:realizable-collision-sign-blocks} are integral and even.  The
+standard block determinant identity gives
+\[
+ \det(I-zB_m)=\det(I-z^2C_m)=Q_m(z^2),
+\]
+while the direct sum gives the second identity in
+\eqref{eq:realizable-collision-determinants}.  Moreover
+\(\abs{B_m},\abs{B_m'}\le A_m\) entrywise and both inequalities are strict
+somewhere.  Since \(A_m\) is positive, the matrices
+\((A_m\pm B_m)/2\) and \((A_m\pm B_m')/2\) realize two cocycles on the same
+marked base, and strict Perron--Frobenius monotonicity gives
+\[
+ \rad(B_m),\rad(B_m')<\rad(A_m)=\lambda_m.
+\]
+
+The \(s_i\) are strictly increasing, so the radii in
+\eqref{eq:realizable-collision-radii} are positive, rational, and distinct.
+The largest is \(4/s_1^2\), and direct expansion gives
+\[
+ s_1^2-4s_m(4m+2)
+ =3008m^2+7136m+4112>0.
+\]
+Thus every \(y_{m,i}<\lambda_m^{-1}\).  The \(i\)-th factor in
+\eqref{eq:realizable-collision-Qm} vanishes at \(y_{m,i}\), so
+\[
+ Q_m(y_{m,i})=1.
+\]
+
+For the sign-determinant ratio in the orientation of
+\Cref{prop:c2-standard-zeta-ratio}, put
+\[
+ H_m(z)=\frac{\det(I-zB_m)}{\det(I-zB_m')}
+ =\frac{Q_m(z^2)}{Q_m(z)^2}.
+\]
+The dyadic identity \eqref{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity} and the
+rational telescope give
+\[
+ F_\varepsilon^{\tau_m}(y)-F_\varepsilon^{\tau_m'}(y)
+ =2\log Q_m(y).
+\]
+It vanishes at every \(y_{m,i}\).  The trivial blocks are both \(A_m\), so
+Fourier inversion for \(C_2\) proves both equalities in
+\eqref{eq:realizable-linear-profile-collisions}.
+
+The polynomial \(Q_m\) is non-constant.  If
+\(Q_m(z^2)=Q_m(z)^2\), comparison of the least non-constant term would give
+two different degrees; hence \(H_m\ne1\).  The comparison dictionary therefore
+shows that the two primitive length--element data sets differ.  Finally,
+\[
+ H_m(z)=
+ \frac{\zeta_{\widetilde X_{\tau_m'}}(z)}
+      {\zeta_{\widetilde X_{\tau_m}}(z)}
+\]
+by \Cref{prop:c2-standard-zeta-ratio}, so these are collisions of standard
+Artin--Mazur zeta ratios.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Linear lower bound for radial determination]
+\label{cor:linear-radial-sampling-lower-bound}
+Let \(\mathsf N_{C_2}(V)\) be the least integer \(N\) such that, for every
+pair of one-step \(C_2\)-cocycles over primitive bases of at most \(V\)
+vertices, equality of both element profiles at \(N\) distinct radii in the
+common open Perron interval, with at least one algebraic radius, forces
+equality of all primitive length--element data.  Then, for \(V\ge6\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:linear-radial-sampling-lower-bound}
+ \mathsf N_{C_2}(V)\ge
+ \left\lfloor\frac{V-2}{4}\right\rfloor+1.
+\end{equation}
+In particular, the worst-case radial sampling complexity is
+\(\Omega(V)\), so the \(O(V\log V)\) upper bound cannot be replaced by
+\(o(V)\).
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Take \(m=\lfloor(V-2)/4\rfloor\), which is positive for \(V\ge6\).
+Then \(4m+2\le V\), and
+\Cref{thm:realizable-linear-multicollisions} gives two distinct periodic-data
+sets agreeing at \(m\) rational radii.  A universal determination number must
+therefore be at least \(m+1\).
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Realizable logarithmic certificate-degree sharpness]
+\label{cor:realizable-logarithmic-certificate-sharpness}
+There is a sequence of pairs of strict-gap \(C_2\)-cocycles on common
+primitive \(V_J\)-vertex bases whose standard Artin--Mazur zeta ratios have
+unique normalized rational Mahler certificates of degree
+\[
+ \frac{V_J}{2}\log_2V_J=\Omega(V_J\log V_J).
+\]
+Thus the \(O(D\log D)\) certificate-degree bound has the correct order even
+on realizable standard \(C_2\)-cover zeta ratios.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Let \(Q(z)=1-2z\), \(J\ge0\), and
+\[
+ R_J(z)=\prod_{j=0}^JQ(z^{2^j})^{2^{J-j}}.
+\]
+As in \Cref{rem:logarithmic-mahler-degree-sharpness},
+\[
+ H_J(z):=\frac{R_J(z^2)}{R_J(z)^2}
+ =\frac{Q(z^{2^{J+1}})}{Q(z)^{2^{J+1}}},
+ \qquad
+ \deg R_J=(J+1)2^J.
+\]
+Put \(V_J=2^{J+1}\).  The numerator and denominator of \(H_J\) have degree
+\(V_J\), constant term one, and are both congruent to one modulo two.
+\Cref{lem:relative-sign-determinant-realization} therefore realizes them as
+the two sign determinants of strict-gap cocycles on one positive
+\(V_J\)-vertex base.  Their ratio is the corresponding standard zeta ratio.
+Normalized injectivity of the Mahler coboundary map makes \(R_J\) its unique
+certificate, and
+\[
+ \deg R_J=(J+1)2^J=\frac{V_J}{2}\log_2V_J.
+\]
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{remark}[Three distinct notions of sharpness]
+\label{rem:three-sharpness-levels}
+\Cref{cor:realizable-logarithmic-certificate-sharpness} concerns certificate
+degree and upgrades the abstract divisor family to standard realizable zeta
+ratios.  It does not produce \(\Omega(V\log V)\) positive real collisions.
+The genuine sampling statement is
+\Cref{cor:linear-radial-sampling-lower-bound}, which gives \(\Omega(V)\)
+distinct rational collisions.  No matching \(\Omega(V\log V)\) positive-real
+sampling lower bound is claimed.
+\end{remark}

+def rational_critical_denominator_audit(order: int = 12) -> dict[str, object]:
+    """Check the (p q)^(2n-1) denominator bound for rational p-products."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    p_zero = 1 + z / 2 + z**2 / 3
+    p_one = 1 - z / 5
+    denominators = [
+        int(sp.denom(coefficient))
+        for polynomial in (p_zero, p_one)
+        for coefficient in sp.Poly(polynomial, z).all_coeffs()
+    ]
+    q = 1
+    for denominator in denominators:
+        q = sp.ilcm(q, denominator)
+
+    all_bounds_hold = True
+    nonintegral_coefficient_seen = False
+    radices = (2, 3, 4, 5)
+    for radix in radices:
+        coefficients = [sp.Integer(1)]
+        for degree in range(1, order + 1):
+            unknown = sp.Symbol(f"f_{degree}")
+            truncated = sum(
+                coefficient * z**index
+                for index, coefficient in enumerate(coefficients)
+            ) + unknown * z**degree
+            coefficient_equation = sp.expand(
+                p_one * truncated**radix
+                - p_zero * truncated.subs(z, z**radix)
+            ).coeff(z, degree)
+            linear_coefficient = coefficient_equation.coeff(unknown)
+            value = sp.cancel(
+                -coefficient_equation.subs(unknown, 0) / linear_coefficient
+            )
+            coefficients.append(value)
+            scaled = sp.cancel((radix * q) ** (2 * degree - 1) * value)
+            all_bounds_hold &= bool(scaled.is_Integer)
+            nonintegral_coefficient_seen |= not bool(value.is_Integer)
+
+        truncated = sum(
+            coefficient * z**index
+            for index, coefficient in enumerate(coefficients)
+        )
+        residual = sp.series(
+            p_one * truncated**radix
+            - p_zero * truncated.subs(z, z**radix),
+            z,
+            0,
+            order + 1,
+        ).removeO()
+        all_bounds_hold &= sp.expand(residual) == 0
+
+    return {
+        "radices": radices,
+        "order": order,
+        "clearing_denominator": q,
+        "all_bounds_hold": all_bounds_hold,
+        "nonintegral_coefficient_seen": nonintegral_coefficient_seen,
+    }
+

+def realizable_multicollision_family_audit(max_m: int = 4) -> dict[str, object]:
+    """Check the parametric standard-cover collision identities exactly."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    vertex_counts: list[int] = []
+    collision_counts: list[int] = []
+    determinant_identities_hold = True
+    all_radii_in_perron_interval = True
+    same_base_realization_holds = True
+    strict_gap_certified = True
+
+    for m in range(1, max_m + 1):
+        n = 2 * m + 1
+        size = 2 * n
+        scales = [64 * (m + 1) + 4 * index for index in range(1, m + 1)]
+        c_matrix = sp.zeros(n)
+        for index, scale in enumerate(scales, 1):
+            c_matrix[index - 1, index] = -4
+            c_matrix[index - 1, m + index] = scale
+            c_matrix[m + index, index] = scale
+        c_matrix[m, 0] = -4
+
+        q_polynomial = sp.expand((sp.eye(n) - z * c_matrix).det())
+        expected_q = sp.expand(
+            1 + 4 * z * sp.prod(-4 * z + scale**2 * z**2 for scale in scales)
+        )
+        first_block = sp.zeros(size)
+        first_block[:n, n:] = c_matrix / 2
+        first_block[n:, :n] = 2 * sp.eye(n)
+        second_block = sp.diag(c_matrix, c_matrix)
+        first_determinant = sp.expand((sp.eye(size) - z * first_block).det())
+        second_determinant = sp.expand((sp.eye(size) - z * second_block).det())
+        determinant_identities_hold &= all(
+            (
+                q_polynomial == expected_q,
+                first_determinant == sp.expand(q_polynomial.subs(z, z**2)),
+                second_determinant == sp.expand(q_polynomial**2),
+            )
+        )
+
+        base_entry = scales[-1]
+        base = sp.ones(size) * base_entry
+        compatibility = all(
+            bool(
+                block[row, column].is_Integer
+                and (base[row, column] - block[row, column]) % 2 == 0
+                and abs(block[row, column]) <= base[row, column]
+            )
+            for block in (first_block, second_block)
+            for row in range(size)
+            for column in range(size)
+        )
+        same_base_realization_holds &= compatibility
+        strict_gap_certified &= all(
+            any(
+                abs(block[row, column]) < base[row, column]
+                for row in range(size)
+                for column in range(size)
+            )
+            for block in (first_block, second_block)
+        )
+
+        radii = tuple(sp.Rational(4, scale**2) for scale in scales)
+        perron_root = base_entry * size
+        all_radii_in_perron_interval &= all(
+            0 < radius < sp.Rational(1, perron_root) for radius in radii
+        )
+        collisions = tuple(
+            radius for radius in radii if q_polynomial.subs(z, radius) == 1
+        )
+        vertex_counts.append(size)
+        collision_counts.append(len(collisions))
+
+    return {
+        "vertex_counts": tuple(vertex_counts),
+        "collision_counts": tuple(collision_counts),
+        "determinant_identities_hold": determinant_identities_hold,
+        "all_radii_in_perron_interval": all_radii_in_perron_interval,
+        "same_base_realization_holds": same_base_realization_holds,
+        "strict_gap_certified": strict_gap_certified,
+    }
+
+
+def _integral_companion_for_reciprocal(polynomial: sp.Expr) -> sp.Matrix:
+    """Return C with det(I-zC)=polynomial for a normalized integral input."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    poly = sp.Poly(polynomial, z)
+    degree = max(1, poly.degree())
+    coefficients = [sp.Integer(poly.nth(index)) for index in range(degree + 1)]
+    companion = sp.zeros(degree)
+    for row in range(1, degree):
+        companion[row, row - 1] = 1
+    for row in range(degree):
+        companion[row, degree - 1] = -coefficients[degree - row]
+    return companion
+

+def realizable_logarithmic_certificate_family_audit(
+    max_depth: int = 4,
+) -> dict[str, object]:
+    """Check companion realizations of the dyadic Omega(V log V) certificates."""
+    z, t = sp.symbols("z t")
+    q_polynomial = 1 - 2 * z
+    vertex_counts: list[int] = []
+    relative_realizations_hold = True
+    certificate_degrees_hold = True
+    zeta_ratios_nontrivial = True
+
+    for depth in range(max_depth + 1):
+        vertex_count = 2 ** (depth + 1)
+        numerator = sp.expand(q_polynomial.subs(z, z**vertex_count))
+        denominator = sp.expand(q_polynomial**vertex_count)
+        first = _integral_companion_for_reciprocal(numerator)
+        second = _integral_companion_for_reciprocal(denominator)
+        same_parity = all(
+            (first[row, column] - second[row, column]) % 2 == 0
+            for row in range(vertex_count)
+            for column in range(vertex_count)
+        )
+
+        base = sp.zeros(vertex_count)
+        for row in range(vertex_count):
+            for column in range(vertex_count):
+                bound = max(abs(first[row, column]), abs(second[row, column]))
+                candidate = int(bound) + 1
+                if candidate % 2 != int(first[row, column]) % 2:
+                    candidate += 1
+                base[row, column] = candidate
+        realizable = same_parity and all(
+            bool(
+                base[row, column] > abs(block[row, column])
+                and (base[row, column] - block[row, column]) % 2 == 0
+            )
+            for block in (first, second)
+            for row in range(vertex_count)
+            for column in range(vertex_count)
+        )
+        expected_first_charpoly = sp.expand(
+            t**vertex_count * numerator.subs(z, 1 / t)
+        )
+        expected_second_charpoly = sp.expand(
+            t**vertex_count * denominator.subs(z, 1 / t)
+        )
+        relative_realizations_hold &= all(
+            (
+                realizable,
+                sp.expand(first.charpoly(t).as_expr())
+                == expected_first_charpoly,
+                sp.expand(second.charpoly(t).as_expr())
+                == expected_second_charpoly,
+            )
+        )
+
+        certificate = sp.prod(
+            q_polynomial.subs(z, z ** (2**index))
+            ** (2 ** (depth - index))
+            for index in range(depth + 1)
+        )
+        certificate_degrees_hold &= (
+            sp.degree(certificate, z)
+            == (depth + 1) * 2**depth
+            == vertex_count * (depth + 1) // 2
+        )
+        zeta_ratios_nontrivial &= sp.cancel(numerator / denominator - 1) != 0
+        vertex_counts.append(vertex_count)
+
+    return {
+        "vertex_counts": tuple(vertex_counts),
+        "relative_realizations_hold": relative_realizations_hold,
+        "certificate_degrees_hold": certificate_degrees_hold,
+        "zeta_ratios_nontrivial": zeta_ratios_nontrivial,
+    }

+\begin{lemma}[Linear-exponent denominators for rational critical products]
+\label{lem:rational-critical-mahler-denominators}
+Let \(p\ge2\), let \(P_0,P_1\in\QQ[z]\) have constant term one, and let
+\(q\ge1\) be an integer for which \(qP_0,qP_1\in\ZZ[z]\).  The unique formal
+series \(F(z)=\sum_{n\ge0}f_nz^n\in1+z\QQ[[z]]\) satisfying
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:rational-critical-mahler-equation}
+ P_1(z)F(z)^p=P_0(z)F(z^p)
+\end{equation}
+obeys
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:rational-critical-mahler-denominator-bound}
+ (pq)^{2n-1}f_n\in\ZZ\qquad(n\ge1).
+\end{equation}
+Consequently the first \(h+1\) coefficients have a common positive
+denominator \(d_h\) satisfying
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:rational-critical-mahler-common-denominator}
+ d_h\mid(pq)^{2h-1},
+ \qquad \log d_h\le(2h-1)\log(pq)\qquad(h\ge1).
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Put \(\widetilde P_i=qP_i\), so that
+\(\widetilde P_i\in\ZZ[z]\) and \(\widetilde P_i(0)=q\).  Comparison of the
+coefficient of \(z^n\) in
+\(\widetilde P_1F^p=\widetilde P_0F(z^p)\) gives
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:rational-critical-mahler-recursion}
+ pqf_n=\Phi_n(f_1,\ldots,f_{n-1}),
+\end{equation}
+where \(\Phi_n\) has integral coefficients.  Indeed, the only occurrence of
+\(f_n\) is obtained by choosing it in one of the \(p\) factors of \(F^p\)
+and constant terms everywhere else.  Every remaining linear term is \(f_j\)
+with \(j<n\); every remaining nonlinear monomial can be written
+\(f_{j_1}\cdots f_{j_s}\), where \(s\ge2\), all \(j_i\ge1\), and
+\(j_1+\cdots+j_s\le n\).
+
+Set \(c=pq\).  We prove \eqref{eq:rational-critical-mahler-denominator-bound}
+by induction.  If it holds below \(n\), a linear term \(f_j\), \(j<n\), has
+denominator dividing \(c^{2j-1}\), hence \(c^{2n-2}\).  A nonlinear monomial
+as above has denominator dividing
+\[
+ c^{\sum_i(2j_i-1)}
+ =c^{2\sum_i j_i-s}\mid c^{2n-2}.
+\]
+Thus \(c^{2n-2}\Phi_n\in\ZZ\), and division by \(c\) in
+\eqref{eq:rational-critical-mahler-recursion} proves the induction step.
+The exponents are increasing with \(n\), so the common-denominator assertion
+and its logarithmic bound follow immediately.
+\end{proof}
+

 it records an effective feature of the critical quadratic equation itself.

+\begin{theorem}[General rational critical \(p\)-Mahler lifting]
+\label{thm:general-rational-p-mahler-lifting}
+Let \(p\ge2\), let \(H\in\QQ(z)^\times\) satisfy \(H(0)=1\), and suppose
+that \(H\) has neither a zero nor a pole on \(\abs z<r\).  On that disk define
+the normalized analytic function
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:general-critical-p-mahler-product}
+ F_{H,p}(z):=\prod_{\nu\ge0}
+ H(z^{p^\nu})^{p^{-\nu-1}},
+ \qquad F_{H,p}(0)=1,
+\end{equation}
+using the logarithm germ at zero.  Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:general-critical-p-mahler-equation}
+ F_{H,p}(z)^p=H(z)F_{H,p}(z^p).
+\end{equation}
+If \(\alpha\ne0\) is algebraic,
+\[
+ \abs\alpha<\min\{r,1\},
+\]
+and \(F_{H,p}(\alpha)\) is algebraic, then there is a unique
+\(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\), normalized by \(R(0)=1\), such that
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:general-critical-p-mahler-lifted-certificate}
+ H(z)=\frac{R(z^p)}{R(z)^p}.
+\end{equation}
+If, in addition, \(0<\alpha<r\) and \(H(t)>0\) on \([0,\alpha]\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:general-critical-p-mahler-positive-equivalence}
+ \prod_{\nu\ge0}H(\alpha^{p^\nu})^{p^{-\nu}}=1
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad R(\alpha)=1.
+\end{equation}
+\end{theorem}

+the elementary denominator estimate

+Keiji Nishioka from 1985, and this coefficient estimate.  We retain
+Dieudonn\'e--Dwork only for the stronger integral conclusion when parity is
+available.  For example, the determinant-realizable subclass remains broad.

+\subsection{Odd-Adams-invariant abelian two-group extensions}
+\label{sec:odd-adams-sampling}
+
+The dyadic reduction extends beyond elementary two-groups precisely when the
+odd Adams directions are constant.  We first record the two algebraic facts
+needed for that extension.
+
+\begin{lemma}[Odd-Adams integrality and M\"obius collapse]
+\label{lem:odd-adams-mobius-collapse}
+Let \(G\) be a finite abelian \(2\)-group and let
+\(\tau:E(\Gamma)\to G\) and \(\tau':E(\Gamma')\to G\) be one-step
+cocycles.  For \(\chi\in\widehat G\), write
+\[
+ P_{\chi,\tau}(z)=\det(I-zA_{\chi,\tau}),\qquad
+ P_{\chi,\tau'}(z)=\det(I-zA_{\chi,\tau'}),
+\]
+and assume, separately for the two cocycles, the condition denoted (OA):
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-adams-determinant-invariance}
+ \begin{aligned}
+ P_{\chi^u,\tau}(z)&=P_{\chi,\tau}(z),\\
+ P_{\chi^u,\tau'}(z)&=P_{\chi,\tau'}(z)
+ \end{aligned}
+ \qquad(\chi\in\widehat G,\ u\ \text{odd}).
+\end{equation}
+Then \(P_{\chi,\tau},P_{\chi,\tau'}\in\ZZ[z]\) for every \(\chi\).
+If
+\[
+ H_\chi(z):=\frac{P_{\chi,\tau}(z)}{P_{\chi,\tau'}(z)},\qquad
+ \Delta_\chi(z):=F_\chi^\tau(z)-F_\chi^{\tau'}(z),
+\]
+then, on the common open Perron disk,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-adams-mobius-collapse}
+ \Delta_\chi(z)
+ =-\sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}\Log_0H_\chi(z^{2^j})
+  +\sum_{j\ge1}2^{-j}\Log_0H_{\chi^2}(z^{2^j}).
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Suppose that \(\chi\) has order \(2^a\), and put
+\(K=\QQ(\chi(G))\).  The entries of \(A_{\chi,\tau}\) lie in the ring of
+integers of \(K\), so the coefficients of \(P_{\chi,\tau}\) are algebraic
+integers.  Every element of \(\operatorname{Gal}(K/\QQ)\) acts on the values
+of \(\chi\) by \(\chi(g)\mapsto\chi(g)^u\) for some odd \(u\), and therefore
+sends \(P_{\chi,\tau}\) to \(P_{\chi^u,\tau}\).  Condition
+\eqref{eq:odd-adams-determinant-invariance} fixes this polynomial under the
+whole Galois group.  Its coefficients are rational algebraic integers, hence
+integers.  The same argument applies to \(\tau'\).
+
+For the collapse, the abelian specialization of
+\eqref{eq:fixed-determinant-open-disc} gives the absolutely convergent identity
+\begin{align}
+ \Delta_\chi(z)
+ &=-\sum_{r,m\ge1}\frac{\mu(m)}{rm}
+      \Log_0H_{\chi^m}(z^{rm})\notag\\
+ &=-\sum_{k\ge1}\frac1k\sum_{m\mid k}\mu(m)
+      \Log_0H_{\chi^m}(z^k).
+ \label{eq:odd-adams-collapse-before-divisors}
+\end{align}
+Write \(k=2^jq\), where \(q\) is odd.  The odd divisors contributing to the
+inner sum have the form \(m=d\), \(d\mid q\), and
+\[
+ \sum_{\substack{m\mid k\\m\ {\rm odd}}}\mu(m)
+ =\sum_{d\mid q}\mu(d)
+ =\begin{cases}1,&q=1,\\0,&q>1.\end{cases}
+\]
+If \(j\ge1\), the square-free even divisors are exactly \(m=2d\), with
+\(d\mid q\) odd, and
+\[
+ \sum_{\substack{m\mid k\\m\ {\rm even}}}\mu(m)
+ =\sum_{d\mid q}\mu(2d)
+ =-\sum_{d\mid q}\mu(d).
+\]
+For odd \(d\), condition (OA) gives
+\[
+ H_{\chi^d}=H_\chi,\qquad
+ H_{\chi^{2d}}=H_{(\chi^2)^d}=H_{\chi^2}.
+\]
+Thus the inner divisor sum in
+\eqref{eq:odd-adams-collapse-before-divisors} vanishes unless \(q=1\);
+for \(k=1\) it is \(\Log_0H_\chi(z)\), and for \(k=2^j\), \(j\ge1\), it is
+\[
+ \Log_0H_\chi(z^{2^j})-\Log_0H_{\chi^2}(z^{2^j}).
+\]
+Substitution proves \eqref{eq:odd-adams-mobius-collapse}.  This is an
+identity of analytic germs, and hence throughout the common Perron disk.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{theorem}[Odd-Adams-invariant finite radial determination]
+\label{thm:odd-adams-abelian-two-group-finite-sampling}
+Let \(G\) be a finite abelian \(2\)-group.  Let
+\(\tau:E(\Gamma)\to G\) and \(\tau':E(\Gamma')\to G\) be one-step
+cocycles over primitive non-negative integral base matrices \(A,A'\), whose
+sizes are at most \(V\) and whose Perron roots are
+\(\lambda,\lambda'>1\).  Assume that both cocycles satisfy (OA) in
+\eqref{eq:odd-adams-determinant-invariance}.  Put
+\[
+ x=\min\{\lambda^{-1},(\lambda')^{-1}\},\qquad
+ M(V)=2V\lceil\log_2(4V)\rceil.
+\]
+For \(g\in G\), define
+\[
+ \mathcal E_g^\tau(y)
+ =\sum_{n\ge1}p_{n,g}(\tau)\log(1-y^n),\qquad 0<y<x,
+\]
+and define \(\mathcal E_g^{\tau'}\) analogously.  Suppose that
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-adams-sampled-profile-equality}
+ \mathcal E_g^\tau(y_i)=\mathcal E_g^{\tau'}(y_i)
+ \qquad(g\in G,\ 1\le i\le M(V))
+\end{equation}
+at \(M(V)\) distinct radii in \((0,x)\), at least one of which is algebraic.
+Then
+\[
+ p_{n,g}(\tau)=p_{n,g}(\tau')
+ \qquad(n\ge1,\ g\in G).
+\]
+The number \(M(V)\) of radial locations is independent of the rank and
+exponent of \(G\), while the total number of scalar equalities in
+\eqref{eq:odd-adams-sampled-profile-equality} is \(\abs G M(V)\).
+Neither a common base nor a strict twisted spectral gap is required.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+All profile series converge absolutely on the stated interval by the
+periodic-point estimate in \Cref{thm:finite-radial-sampling}.  Summing
+\eqref{eq:odd-adams-sampled-profile-equality} over \(g\) gives
+\[
+ \log\det(I-y_iA)=\log\det(I-y_iA')
+ \qquad(1\le i\le M(V)).
+\]
+The determinants are positive on \((0,x)\).  Their difference has degree at
+most \(V\), vanishes at the sampled radii and at zero, and hence is zero:
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-adams-base-determinant-equality}
+ P_{\mathbf1,\tau}(z)=\det(I-zA)=\det(I-zA')
+ =P_{\mathbf1,\tau'}(z).
+\end{equation}
+Thus \(H_{\mathbf1}=1\).
+
+Fourier transformation of the sampled element-profile equalities gives
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-adams-sampled-fourier-equality}
+ \Delta_\chi(y_i)
+ =-\sum_{g\in G}\chi(g)
+   \bigl(\mathcal E_g^\tau(y_i)-\mathcal E_g^{\tau'}(y_i)\bigr)
+ =0
+\end{equation}
+for every \(\chi\in\widehat G\) and every \(i\).  We prove
+\(H_\chi=1\) by induction on the order of \(\chi\).  The order-one case is
+\eqref{eq:odd-adams-base-determinant-equality}.  Assume the assertion for
+all characters of order less than \(2^a\), and let \(\chi\) have order
+\(2^a\).  Then \(H_{\chi^2}=1\), so
+\Cref{lem:odd-adams-mobius-collapse} reduces to
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-adams-inductive-dyadic-orbit}
+ \Delta_\chi(y)
+ =-\sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}\log H_\chi(y^{2^j})
+ \qquad(0<y<x).
+\end{equation}
+
+By \Cref{lem:odd-adams-mobius-collapse}, \(H_\chi\in\QQ(z)^\times\).
+Entrywise,
+\[
+ \abs{(A_{\chi,\tau})_{uv}}\le A_{uv},\qquad
+ \abs{(A_{\chi,\tau'})_{uv}}\le A'_{uv}.
+\]
+Perron-weighted domination therefore makes both character determinants
+zero-free on their open Perron disks.  Since they are real polynomials with
+value one at zero, they and \(H_\chi\) are positive on \((0,x)\).
+
+Choose an algebraic sampled radius \(y_0\).  Equations
+\eqref{eq:odd-adams-sampled-fourier-equality} and
+\eqref{eq:odd-adams-inductive-dyadic-orbit} give
+\[
+ \prod_{j\ge0}H_\chi(y_0^{2^j})^{2^{-j}}=1.
+\]
+If \(H_\chi\ne1\), \Cref{thm:general-rational-p-mahler-lifting} with \(p=2\)
+gives the unique normalized \(R_\chi\in\QQ(z)^\times\) such that
+\[
+ H_\chi(z)=\frac{R_\chi(z^2)}{R_\chi(z)^2},\qquad R_\chi(y_0)=1.
+\]
+Write \(H_\chi=P_{0,\chi}/P_{1,\chi}\) in reduced form and put
+\(D_\chi=\deg P_{0,\chi}+\deg P_{1,\chi}\).  Both determinants have degree
+at most \(V\), so \(D_\chi\le2V\).  The rational telescope and
+\Cref{prop:logarithmic-mahler-divisor-bound} show that every real zero of
+\(\Delta_\chi\) is a non-zero root of \(R_\chi-1\), and that there are at
+most
+\[
+ b_2(D_\chi)-1
+ =D_\chi\lceil\log_2(2D_\chi)\rceil-1
+ \le M(V)-1
+\]
+such roots.  This contradicts the \(M(V)\) distinct zeros in
+\eqref{eq:odd-adams-sampled-fourier-equality}.  Hence \(H_\chi=1\), closing
+the induction.
+
+All character determinants now agree between the two systems.  The
+cross-base periodic-data dictionary in \Cref{prop:comparison-dictionary},
+followed by Fourier inversion on \(G\), recovers every
+\(p_{n,g}\), as asserted.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{remark}[Concrete scope of (OA)]
+\label{rem:odd-adams-concrete-scope}
+Condition (OA) is automatic for \(G=(C_2)^r\).  A stronger entrywise
+sufficient condition for a general abelian \(2\)-group is that, for every
+ordered vertex pair, every \(g\in G\), and every odd \(u\), the number of
+\(g\)-labelled edges equals the number of \(g^u\)-labelled edges.  It then
+gives \(A_{\chi^u}=A_\chi\), not merely equality of their determinants.
+
+For \(C_4=\langle a\rangle\), this condition says exactly that the
+\(a\)- and \(a^{-1}\)-labelled edge counts agree entrywise; the \(e\)- and
+\(a^2\)-counts are unrestricted.  It does not force factorization through
+\(C_2\): a one-vertex graph with equally many \(a\)- and \(a^{-1}\)-loops
+has primitive base and holonomy subgroup \(C_4\).  Likewise, assigning equal
+counts on each odd-power orbit in \(C_{2^s}\) gives examples with genuine
+holonomy of order \(2^s\).
+\end{remark}

+\subsection{Realizable collision and certificate lower bounds}
+\label{sec:realizable-collision-lower-bounds}
+
+We begin with a relative realization fact for sign determinants.  It is
+sufficient for both the explicit collision family and the abstract
+certificate-degree family.
+
+\begin{lemma}[Relative sign-determinant realization]
+\label{lem:relative-sign-determinant-realization}
+Let \(P_0,P_1\in\ZZ[z]\) satisfy
+\[
+ P_0(0)=P_1(0)=1,\qquad P_0\equiv P_1\pmod2.
+\]
+Put \(d=\max\{1,\deg P_0,\deg P_1\}\).  There are a positive integral
+\(d\times d\) matrix \(A\) and two one-step \(C_2\)-cocycles on the same
+marked base graph with sign blocks \(C_0,C_1\) such that
+\[
+ \det(I-zC_i)=P_i(z)\qquad(i=0,1),
+\]
+and both sign blocks have strict twisted spectral gap:
+\[
+ \rad(C_i)<\rad(A)\qquad(i=0,1).
+\]
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Pad both polynomials to degree \(d\), and let \(C_i\) be the integral
+companion matrix of the monic polynomial
+\[
+ t^dP_i(t^{-1}).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ \det(I-zC_i)=z^d\det(z^{-1}I-C_i)=P_i(z).
+\]
+The congruence of the polynomials makes the two standard companion matrices
+entrywise congruent modulo two.  For each entry choose a positive integer
+\(A_{jk}\), in this common parity class, with
+\[
+ A_{jk}>\max\{\abs{(C_0)_{jk}},\abs{(C_1)_{jk}}\}.
+\]
+Thus \(A\) is positive and hence primitive.  For each \(i\), the non-negative
+integral matrices
+\[
+ \frac{A+C_i}{2},\qquad \frac{A-C_i}{2}
+\]
+count respectively the \(e\)- and \(s\)-labelled edges of a \(C_2\)-cocycle
+on this same marked base.  Finally,
+\[
+ \rad(C_i)\le\rad(\abs{C_i})<\rad(A)
+\]
+by strict Perron--Frobenius monotonicity, proving the gap.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{theorem}[Realizable linear multi-collisions]
+\label{thm:realizable-linear-multicollisions}
+For every integer \(m\ge1\), there is a positive primitive directed
+multigraph with
+\[
+ v_m=4m+2
+\]
+vertices and two one-step \(C_2\)-cocycles \(\tau_m,\tau_m'\) on the same
+marked base, both with strict twisted spectral gap, for which the primitive
+length--element data differ but
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:realizable-linear-profile-collisions}
+ \mathcal E_e^{\tau_m}(y_{m,i})
+ =\mathcal E_e^{\tau_m'}(y_{m,i}),\qquad
+ \mathcal E_s^{\tau_m}(y_{m,i})
+ =\mathcal E_s^{\tau_m'}(y_{m,i})
+ \quad(1\le i\le m)
+\end{equation}
+at \(m\) distinct rational radii in the open Perron interval.
+
+More explicitly, put
+\[
+ s_i=64(m+1)+4i\qquad(1\le i\le m)
+\]
+and let \(C_m\) be the \((2m+1)\times(2m+1)\) integral matrix indexed by
+\[
+ u_0,\ldots,u_m,w_1,\ldots,w_m
+\]
+whose only non-zero entries are
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:realizable-collision-Cm-entries}
+ \begin{aligned}
+  (C_m)_{u_{i-1},u_i}&=-4,&
+  (C_m)_{u_{i-1},w_i}&=s_i &&(1\le i\le m),\\
+  (C_m)_{w_i,u_i}&=s_i,&
+  (C_m)_{u_m,u_0}&=-4.
+ \end{aligned}
+\end{equation}
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:realizable-collision-Qm}
+ Q_m(z):=\det(I-zC_m)
+ =1+4z\prod_{i=1}^m(-4z+s_i^2z^2).
+\end{equation}
+Writing \(n=2m+1\), take the two \(2n\times2n\) sign blocks
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:realizable-collision-sign-blocks}
+ B_m=\begin{pmatrix}0&C_m/2\\2I_n&0\end{pmatrix},
+ \qquad B_m'=C_m\oplus C_m.
+\end{equation}
+They satisfy
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:realizable-collision-determinants}
+ \det(I-zB_m)=Q_m(z^2),\qquad
+ \det(I-zB_m')=Q_m(z)^2.
+\end{equation}
+The common base may be chosen as
+\[
+ A_m=s_mJ_{4m+2},\qquad
+ \lambda_m=s_m(4m+2),
+\]
+and the collision radii are
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:realizable-collision-radii}
+ y_{m,i}=\frac4{s_i^2}\qquad(1\le i\le m).
+\end{equation}
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+In the directed support of \(C_m\), every non-trivial cycle must traverse
+from \(u_0\) through the stages \(1,\ldots,m\) and then use the closing edge
+\(u_m\to u_0\).  At stage \(i\), it uses either the direct edge of weight
+\(-4\), contributing \(-4z\), or the two-edge detour through \(w_i\),
+contributing \(s_i^2z^2\).  A single directed cycle contributes the negative
+of the product of its weighted \(z\)-edges to \(\det(I-zC_m)\).  The closing
+edge contributes \(-4z\), so summing the \(2^m\) choices gives
+\[
+ 1-(-4z)\prod_{i=1}^m(-4z+s_i^2z^2),
+\]
+which is \eqref{eq:realizable-collision-Qm}.
+
+All entries of \(C_m\) are divisible by four.  Hence the blocks in
+\eqref{eq:realizable-collision-sign-blocks} are integral and even.  The
+standard block determinant identity gives
+\[
+ \det(I-zB_m)=\det(I-z^2C_m)=Q_m(z^2),
+\]
+while the direct sum gives the second identity in
+\eqref{eq:realizable-collision-determinants}.  Moreover
+\(\abs{B_m},\abs{B_m'}\le A_m\) entrywise and both inequalities are strict
+somewhere.  Since \(A_m\) is positive, the matrices
+\((A_m\pm B_m)/2\) and \((A_m\pm B_m')/2\) realize two cocycles on the same
+marked base, and strict Perron--Frobenius monotonicity gives
+\[
+ \rad(B_m),\rad(B_m')<\rad(A_m)=\lambda_m.
+\]
+
+The \(s_i\) are strictly increasing, so the radii in
+\eqref{eq:realizable-collision-radii} are positive, rational, and distinct.
+The largest is \(4/s_1^2\), and direct expansion gives
+\[
+ s_1^2-4s_m(4m+2)
+ =3008m^2+7136m+4112>0.
+\]
+Thus every \(y_{m,i}<\lambda_m^{-1}\).  The \(i\)-th factor in
+\eqref{eq:realizable-collision-Qm} vanishes at \(y_{m,i}\), so
+\[
+ Q_m(y_{m,i})=1.
+\]
+
+For the sign-determinant ratio in the orientation of
+\Cref{prop:c2-standard-zeta-ratio}, put
+\[
+ H_m(z)=\frac{\det(I-zB_m)}{\det(I-zB_m')}
+ =\frac{Q_m(z^2)}{Q_m(z)^2}.
+\]
+The dyadic identity \eqref{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity} and the
+rational telescope give
+\[
+ F_\varepsilon^{\tau_m}(y)-F_\varepsilon^{\tau_m'}(y)
+ =2\log Q_m(y).
+\]
+It vanishes at every \(y_{m,i}\).  The trivial blocks are both \(A_m\), so
+Fourier inversion for \(C_2\) proves both equalities in
+\eqref{eq:realizable-linear-profile-collisions}.
+
+The polynomial \(Q_m\) is non-constant.  If
+\(Q_m(z^2)=Q_m(z)^2\), comparison of the least non-constant term would give
+two different degrees; hence \(H_m\ne1\).  The comparison dictionary therefore
+shows that the two primitive length--element data sets differ.  Finally,
+\[
+ H_m(z)=
+ \frac{\zeta_{\widetilde X_{\tau_m'}}(z)}
+      {\zeta_{\widetilde X_{\tau_m}}(z)}
+\]
+by \Cref{prop:c2-standard-zeta-ratio}, so these are collisions of standard
+Artin--Mazur zeta ratios.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Linear lower bound for radial determination]
+\label{cor:linear-radial-sampling-lower-bound}
+Let \(\mathsf N_{C_2}(V)\) be the least integer \(N\) such that, for every
+pair of one-step \(C_2\)-cocycles over primitive bases of at most \(V\)
+vertices, equality of both element profiles at \(N\) distinct radii in the
+common open Perron interval, with at least one algebraic radius, forces
+equality of all primitive length--element data.  Then, for \(V\ge6\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:linear-radial-sampling-lower-bound}
+ \mathsf N_{C_2}(V)\ge
+ \left\lfloor\frac{V-2}{4}\right\rfloor+1.
+\end{equation}
+In particular, the worst-case radial sampling complexity is
+\(\Omega(V)\), so the \(O(V\log V)\) upper bound cannot be replaced by
+\(o(V)\).
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Take \(m=\lfloor(V-2)/4\rfloor\), which is positive for \(V\ge6\).
+Then \(4m+2\le V\), and
+\Cref{thm:realizable-linear-multicollisions} gives two distinct periodic-data
+sets agreeing at \(m\) rational radii.  A universal determination number must
+therefore be at least \(m+1\).
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Realizable logarithmic certificate-degree sharpness]
+\label{cor:realizable-logarithmic-certificate-sharpness}
+There is a sequence of pairs of strict-gap \(C_2\)-cocycles on common
+primitive \(V_J\)-vertex bases whose standard Artin--Mazur zeta ratios have
+unique normalized rational Mahler certificates of degree
+\[
+ \frac{V_J}{2}\log_2V_J=\Omega(V_J\log V_J).
+\]
+Thus the \(O(D\log D)\) certificate-degree bound has the correct order even
+on realizable standard \(C_2\)-cover zeta ratios.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Let \(Q(z)=1-2z\), \(J\ge0\), and
+\[
+ R_J(z)=\prod_{j=0}^JQ(z^{2^j})^{2^{J-j}}.
+\]
+As in \Cref{rem:logarithmic-mahler-degree-sharpness},
+\[
+ H_J(z):=\frac{R_J(z^2)}{R_J(z)^2}
+ =\frac{Q(z^{2^{J+1}})}{Q(z)^{2^{J+1}}},
+ \qquad
+ \deg R_J=(J+1)2^J.
+\]
+Put \(V_J=2^{J+1}\).  The numerator and denominator of \(H_J\) have degree
+\(V_J\), constant term one, and are both congruent to one modulo two.
+\Cref{lem:relative-sign-determinant-realization} therefore realizes them as
+the two sign determinants of strict-gap cocycles on one positive
+\(V_J\)-vertex base.  Their ratio is the corresponding standard zeta ratio.
+Normalized injectivity of the Mahler coboundary map makes \(R_J\) its unique
+certificate, and
+\[
+ \deg R_J=(J+1)2^J=\frac{V_J}{2}\log_2V_J.
+\]
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{remark}[Three distinct notions of sharpness]
+\label{rem:three-sharpness-levels}
+\Cref{cor:realizable-logarithmic-certificate-sharpness} concerns certificate
+degree and upgrades the abstract divisor family to standard realizable zeta
+ratios.  It does not produce \(\Omega(V\log V)\) positive real collisions.
+The genuine sampling statement is
+\Cref{cor:linear-radial-sampling-lower-bound}, which gives \(\Omega(V)\)
+distinct rational collisions.  No matching \(\Omega(V\log V)\) positive-real
+sampling lower bound is claimed.
+\end{remark}

+def rational_critical_denominator_audit(order: int = 12) -> dict[str, object]:
+    """Check the (p q)^(2n-1) denominator bound for rational p-products."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    p_zero = 1 + z / 2 + z**2 / 3
+    p_one = 1 - z / 5
+    denominators = [
+        int(sp.denom(coefficient))
+        for polynomial in (p_zero, p_one)
+        for coefficient in sp.Poly(polynomial, z).all_coeffs()
+    ]
+    q = 1
+    for denominator in denominators:
+        q = sp.ilcm(q, denominator)
+
+    all_bounds_hold = True
+    nonintegral_coefficient_seen = False
+    radices = (2, 3, 4, 5)
+    for radix in radices:
+        coefficients = [sp.Integer(1)]
+        for degree in range(1, order + 1):
+            unknown = sp.Symbol(f"f_{degree}")
+            truncated = sum(
+                coefficient * z**index
+                for index, coefficient in enumerate(coefficients)
+            ) + unknown * z**degree
+            coefficient_equation = sp.expand(
+                p_one * truncated**radix
+                - p_zero * truncated.subs(z, z**radix)
+            ).coeff(z, degree)
+            linear_coefficient = coefficient_equation.coeff(unknown)
+            value = sp.cancel(
+                -coefficient_equation.subs(unknown, 0) / linear_coefficient
+            )
+            coefficients.append(value)
+            scaled = sp.cancel((radix * q) ** (2 * degree - 1) * value)
+            all_bounds_hold &= bool(scaled.is_Integer)
+            nonintegral_coefficient_seen |= not bool(value.is_Integer)
+
+        truncated = sum(
+            coefficient * z**index
+            for index, coefficient in enumerate(coefficients)
+        )
+        residual = sp.series(
+            p_one * truncated**radix
+            - p_zero * truncated.subs(z, z**radix),
+            z,
+            0,
+            order + 1,
+        ).removeO()
+        all_bounds_hold &= sp.expand(residual) == 0
+
+    return {
+        "radices": radices,
+        "order": order,
+        "clearing_denominator": q,
+        "all_bounds_hold": all_bounds_hold,
+        "nonintegral_coefficient_seen": nonintegral_coefficient_seen,
+    }
+

+def realizable_multicollision_family_audit(max_m: int = 4) -> dict[str, object]:
+    """Check the parametric standard-cover collision identities exactly."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    vertex_counts: list[int] = []
+    collision_counts: list[int] = []
+    determinant_identities_hold = True
+    all_radii_in_perron_interval = True
+    same_base_realization_holds = True
+    strict_gap_certified = True
+
+    for m in range(1, max_m + 1):
+        n = 2 * m + 1
+        size = 2 * n
+        scales = [64 * (m + 1) + 4 * index for index in range(1, m + 1)]
+        c_matrix = sp.zeros(n)
+        for index, scale in enumerate(scales, 1):
+            c_matrix[index - 1, index] = -4
+            c_matrix[index - 1, m + index] = scale
+            c_matrix[m + index, index] = scale
+        c_matrix[m, 0] = -4
+
+        q_polynomial = sp.expand((sp.eye(n) - z * c_matrix).det())
+        expected_q = sp.expand(
+            1 + 4 * z * sp.prod(-4 * z + scale**2 * z**2 for scale in scales)
+        )
+        first_block = sp.zeros(size)
+        first_block[:n, n:] = c_matrix / 2
+        first_block[n:, :n] = 2 * sp.eye(n)
+        second_block = sp.diag(c_matrix, c_matrix)
+        first_determinant = sp.expand((sp.eye(size) - z * first_block).det())
+        second_determinant = sp.expand((sp.eye(size) - z * second_block).det())
+        determinant_identities_hold &= all(
+            (
+                q_polynomial == expected_q,
+                first_determinant == sp.expand(q_polynomial.subs(z, z**2)),
+                second_determinant == sp.expand(q_polynomial**2),
+            )
+        )
+
+        base_entry = scales[-1]
+        base = sp.ones(size) * base_entry
+        compatibility = all(
+            bool(
+                block[row, column].is_Integer
+                and (base[row, column] - block[row, column]) % 2 == 0
+                and abs(block[row, column]) <= base[row, column]
+            )
+            for block in (first_block, second_block)
+            for row in range(size)
+            for column in range(size)
+        )
+        same_base_realization_holds &= compatibility
+        strict_gap_certified &= all(
+            any(
+                abs(block[row, column]) < base[row, column]
+                for row in range(size)
+                for column in range(size)
+            )
+            for block in (first_block, second_block)
+        )
+
+        radii = tuple(sp.Rational(4, scale**2) for scale in scales)
+        perron_root = base_entry * size
+        all_radii_in_perron_interval &= all(
+            0 < radius < sp.Rational(1, perron_root) for radius in radii
+        )
+        collisions = tuple(
+            radius for radius in radii if q_polynomial.subs(z, radius) == 1
+        )
+        vertex_counts.append(size)
+        collision_counts.append(len(collisions))
+
+    return {
+        "vertex_counts": tuple(vertex_counts),
+        "collision_counts": tuple(collision_counts),
+        "determinant_identities_hold": determinant_identities_hold,
+        "all_radii_in_perron_interval": all_radii_in_perron_interval,
+        "same_base_realization_holds": same_base_realization_holds,
+        "strict_gap_certified": strict_gap_certified,
+    }
+
+
+def _integral_companion_for_reciprocal(polynomial: sp.Expr) -> sp.Matrix:
+    """Return C with det(I-zC)=polynomial for a normalized integral input."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    poly = sp.Poly(polynomial, z)
+    degree = max(1, poly.degree())
+    coefficients = [sp.Integer(poly.nth(index)) for index in range(degree + 1)]
+    companion = sp.zeros(degree)
+    for row in range(1, degree):
+        companion[row, row - 1] = 1
+    for row in range(degree):
+        companion[row, degree - 1] = -coefficients[degree - row]
+    return companion
+

+def realizable_logarithmic_certificate_family_audit(
+    max_depth: int = 4,
+) -> dict[str, object]:
+    """Check companion realizations of the dyadic Omega(V log V) certificates."""
+    z, t = sp.symbols("z t")
+    q_polynomial = 1 - 2 * z
+    vertex_counts: list[int] = []
+    relative_realizations_hold = True
+    certificate_degrees_hold = True
+    zeta_ratios_nontrivial = True
+
+    for depth in range(max_depth + 1):
+        vertex_count = 2 ** (depth + 1)
+        numerator = sp.expand(q_polynomial.subs(z, z**vertex_count))
+        denominator = sp.expand(q_polynomial**vertex_count)
+        first = _integral_companion_for_reciprocal(numerator)
+        second = _integral_companion_for_reciprocal(denominator)
+        same_parity = all(
+            (first[row, column] - second[row, column]) % 2 == 0
+            for row in range(vertex_count)
+            for column in range(vertex_count)
+        )
+
+        base = sp.zeros(vertex_count)
+        for row in range(vertex_count):
+            for column in range(vertex_count):
+                bound = max(abs(first[row, column]), abs(second[row, column]))
+                candidate = int(bound) + 1
+                if candidate % 2 != int(first[row, column]) % 2:
+                    candidate += 1
+                base[row, column] = candidate
+        realizable = same_parity and all(
+            bool(
+                base[row, column] > abs(block[row, column])
+                and (base[row, column] - block[row, column]) % 2 == 0
+            )
+            for block in (first, second)
+            for row in range(vertex_count)
+            for column in range(vertex_count)
+        )
+        expected_first_charpoly = sp.expand(
+            t**vertex_count * numerator.subs(z, 1 / t)
+        )
+        expected_second_charpoly = sp.expand(
+            t**vertex_count * denominator.subs(z, 1 / t)
+        )
+        relative_realizations_hold &= all(
+            (
+                realizable,
+                sp.expand(first.charpoly(t).as_expr())
+                == expected_first_charpoly,
+                sp.expand(second.charpoly(t).as_expr())
+                == expected_second_charpoly,
+            )
+        )
+
+        certificate = sp.prod(
+            q_polynomial.subs(z, z ** (2**index))
+            ** (2 ** (depth - index))
+            for index in range(depth + 1)
+        )
+        certificate_degrees_hold &= (
+            sp.degree(certificate, z)
+            == (depth + 1) * 2**depth
+            == vertex_count * (depth + 1) // 2
+        )
+        zeta_ratios_nontrivial &= sp.cancel(numerator / denominator - 1) != 0
+        vertex_counts.append(vertex_count)
+
+    return {
+        "vertex_counts": tuple(vertex_counts),
+        "relative_realizations_hold": relative_realizations_hold,
+        "certificate_degrees_hold": certificate_degrees_hold,
+        "zeta_ratios_nontrivial": zeta_ratios_nontrivial,
+    }

+\begin{lemma}[Linear-exponent denominators for rational critical products]
+\label{lem:rational-critical-mahler-denominators}
+Let \(p\ge2\), let \(P_0,P_1\in\QQ[z]\) have constant term one, and let
+\(q\ge1\) be an integer for which \(qP_0,qP_1\in\ZZ[z]\).  The unique formal
+series \(F(z)=\sum_{n\ge0}f_nz^n\in1+z\QQ[[z]]\) satisfying
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:rational-critical-mahler-equation}
+ P_1(z)F(z)^p=P_0(z)F(z^p)
+\end{equation}
+obeys
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:rational-critical-mahler-denominator-bound}
+ (pq)^{2n-1}f_n\in\ZZ\qquad(n\ge1).
+\end{equation}
+Consequently the first \(h+1\) coefficients have a common positive
+denominator \(d_h\) satisfying
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:rational-critical-mahler-common-denominator}
+ d_h\mid(pq)^{2h-1},
+ \qquad \log d_h\le(2h-1)\log(pq)\qquad(h\ge1).
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Put \(\widetilde P_i=qP_i\), so that
+\(\widetilde P_i\in\ZZ[z]\) and \(\widetilde P_i(0)=q\).  Comparison of the
+coefficient of \(z^n\) in
+\(\widetilde P_1F^p=\widetilde P_0F(z^p)\) gives
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:rational-critical-mahler-recursion}
+ pqf_n=\Phi_n(f_1,\ldots,f_{n-1}),
+\end{equation}
+where \(\Phi_n\) has integral coefficients.  Indeed, the only occurrence of
+\(f_n\) is obtained by choosing it in one of the \(p\) factors of \(F^p\)
+and constant terms everywhere else.  Every remaining linear term is \(f_j\)
+with \(j<n\); every remaining nonlinear monomial can be written
+\(f_{j_1}\cdots f_{j_s}\), where \(s\ge2\), all \(j_i\ge1\), and
+\(j_1+\cdots+j_s\le n\).
+
+Set \(c=pq\).  We prove \eqref{eq:rational-critical-mahler-denominator-bound}
+by induction.  If it holds below \(n\), a linear term \(f_j\), \(j<n\), has
+denominator dividing \(c^{2j-1}\), hence \(c^{2n-2}\).  A nonlinear monomial
+as above has denominator dividing
+\[
+ c^{\sum_i(2j_i-1)}
+ =c^{2\sum_i j_i-s}\mid c^{2n-2}.
+\]
+Thus \(c^{2n-2}\Phi_n\in\ZZ\), and division by \(c\) in
+\eqref{eq:rational-critical-mahler-recursion} proves the induction step.
+The exponents are increasing with \(n\), so the common-denominator assertion
+and its logarithmic bound follow immediately.
+\end{proof}
+

+\begin{theorem}[General rational critical \(p\)-Mahler lifting]
+\label{thm:general-rational-p-mahler-lifting}
+Let \(p\ge2\), let \(H\in\QQ(z)^\times\) satisfy \(H(0)=1\), and suppose
+that \(H\) has neither a zero nor a pole on \(\abs z<r\).  On that disk define
+the normalized analytic function
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:general-critical-p-mahler-product}
+ F_{H,p}(z):=\prod_{\nu\ge0}
+ H(z^{p^\nu})^{p^{-\nu-1}},
+ \qquad F_{H,p}(0)=1,
+\end{equation}
+using the logarithm germ at zero.  Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:general-critical-p-mahler-equation}
+ F_{H,p}(z)^p=H(z)F_{H,p}(z^p).
+\end{equation}
+If \(\alpha\ne0\) is algebraic,
+\[
+ \abs\alpha<\min\{r,1\},
+\]
+and \(F_{H,p}(\alpha)\) is algebraic, then there is a unique
+\(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\), normalized by \(R(0)=1\), such that
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:general-critical-p-mahler-lifted-certificate}
+ H(z)=\frac{R(z^p)}{R(z)^p}.
+\end{equation}
+If, in addition, \(0<\alpha<r\) and \(H(t)>0\) on \([0,\alpha]\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:general-critical-p-mahler-positive-equivalence}
+ \prod_{\nu\ge0}H(\alpha^{p^\nu})^{p^{-\nu}}=1
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad R(\alpha)=1.
+\end{equation}
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The logarithmic series in \eqref{eq:general-critical-p-mahler-product}
+converges normally on compact subdisks because
+\(\Log_0H(z)=O(z)\).  It defines a non-vanishing analytic function, and
+shifting the series proves \eqref{eq:general-critical-p-mahler-equation}.
+
+Write \(H=P_0/P_1\) in reduced form with
+\(P_0,P_1\in\QQ[z]\) and \(P_0(0)=P_1(0)=1\), and choose \(q\ge1\) clearing
+their coefficients.  If
+\(F_{H,p}(z)=\sum_{h\ge0}f_hz^h\), then
+\Cref{lem:rational-critical-mahler-denominators} gives the exact estimate
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:general-critical-p-mahler-denominator-input}
+ (pq)^{2h-1}f_h\in\ZZ,\qquad
+ \log d_h\le(2h-1)\log(pq),
+\end{equation}
+where \(d_h\) is a common denominator for \(f_0,\ldots,f_h\).  Choose
+\(s\) with \(\abs\alpha<s<\min\{r,1\}\).  Cauchy's estimate gives
+\[
+ \abs{f_h}\le
+ \max_{\abs z=s}\abs{F_{H,p}(z)}\,s^{-h}.
+\]
+Together with \eqref{eq:general-critical-p-mahler-denominator-input}, this
+also bounds the logarithmic height of \(f_h\) linearly in \(h\).
+
+We may now apply Kumiko Nishioka's printed special-value theorem
+\cite[Theorem, p.~387]{Nishioka1982MahlerFunctionValues}.  For completeness,
+we check its parameters and orbit hypotheses.  In that theorem take
+\[
+ Tz=z^p,\qquad
+ Q_0(z,u)=P_0(z),\qquad Q_1(z,u)=-P_1(z)u^p.
+\]
+The two \(Q_i\) are relatively prime in
+\(\overline{\QQ}[z,u]\), and its auxiliary polynomial may be chosen as
+\(g(z)=P_0(z)\).  The numerical parameters are
+\[
+ N=0,\qquad n=1,\qquad m=p,\qquad M=p,\qquad U=1,\qquad L=1.
+\]
+The coefficient-size and common-denominator hypotheses with \(L=1\) are
+exactly the bounds just proved, and the required strict inequality is
+\[
+ M(p+N)n^2=p^2<p^{2+1/L}=p^3.
 \]
-Normalized injectivity in \Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate} proves
-uniqueness.  The rationality implication used here is Keiji Nishioka's theorem;
-the only descent specific to the present normalization is from the rational
-Taylor germ to \(\QQ(z)\).
+Moreover \(T^i\alpha=\alpha^{p^i}\ne0\), and
+\(g(T^i\alpha)=P_0(\alpha^{p^i})\ne0\) for every \(i\), because
+\(\abs{\alpha^{p^i}}\le\abs\alpha<r\) and \(H\) is zero-free there.
+The product is analytic at every point of this orbit.  Thus the cited theorem
+implies that a transcendental \(F_{H,p}\) has transcendental value at
+\(\alpha\).  The assumed algebraicity of \(F_{H,p}(\alpha)\) therefore makes
+\(F_{H,p}\) algebraic over \(\CC(z)\).
+
+\Cref{prop:algebraic-mahler-coboundary} now gives the unique normalized
+rational function \(R=F_{H,p}^{-1}\) and
+\eqref{eq:general-critical-p-mahler-lifted-certificate}.  Under the final
+positivity assumptions, the branch in
+\eqref{eq:general-critical-p-mahler-product} is positive on
+\([0,\alpha]\), so \(R(\alpha)>0\), and
+\[
+ \prod_{\nu\ge0}H(\alpha^{p^\nu})^{p^{-\nu}}
+ =F_{H,p}(\alpha)^p=R(\alpha)^{-p}.
+\]
+This proves \eqref{eq:general-critical-p-mahler-positive-equivalence}.
 \end{proof}

+the elementary denominator estimate

+special-value theorem, the cited algebraic-solution rationality result of
+Keiji Nishioka from 1985, and this coefficient estimate.  We retain
+Dieudonn\'e--Dwork only for the stronger integral conclusion when parity is
+available.  For example, the determinant-realizable subclass remains broad.

+\subsection{Odd-Adams-invariant abelian two-group extensions}
+\label{sec:odd-adams-sampling}
+
+The dyadic reduction extends beyond elementary two-groups precisely when the
+odd Adams directions are constant.  We first record the two algebraic facts
+needed for that extension.
+
+\begin{lemma}[Odd-Adams integrality and M\"obius collapse]
+\label{lem:odd-adams-mobius-collapse}
+Let \(G\) be a finite abelian \(2\)-group and let
+\(\tau:E(\Gamma)\to G\) and \(\tau':E(\Gamma')\to G\) be one-step
+cocycles.  For \(\chi\in\widehat G\), write
+\[
+ P_{\chi,\tau}(z)=\det(I-zA_{\chi,\tau}),\qquad
+ P_{\chi,\tau'}(z)=\det(I-zA_{\chi,\tau'}),
+\]
+and assume, separately for the two cocycles, the condition denoted (OA):
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-adams-determinant-invariance}
+ \begin{aligned}
+ P_{\chi^u,\tau}(z)&=P_{\chi,\tau}(z),\\
+ P_{\chi^u,\tau'}(z)&=P_{\chi,\tau'}(z)
+ \end{aligned}
+ \qquad(\chi\in\widehat G,\ u\ \text{odd}).
+\end{equation}
+Then \(P_{\chi,\tau},P_{\chi,\tau'}\in\ZZ[z]\) for every \(\chi\).
+If
+\[
+ H_\chi(z):=\frac{P_{\chi,\tau}(z)}{P_{\chi,\tau'}(z)},\qquad
+ \Delta_\chi(z):=F_\chi^\tau(z)-F_\chi^{\tau'}(z),
+\]
+then, on the common open Perron disk,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-adams-mobius-collapse}
+ \Delta_\chi(z)
+ =-\sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}\Log_0H_\chi(z^{2^j})
+  +\sum_{j\ge1}2^{-j}\Log_0H_{\chi^2}(z^{2^j}).
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Suppose that \(\chi\) has order \(2^a\), and put
+\(K=\QQ(\chi(G))\).  The entries of \(A_{\chi,\tau}\) lie in the ring of
+integers of \(K\), so the coefficients of \(P_{\chi,\tau}\) are algebraic
+integers.  Every element of \(\operatorname{Gal}(K/\QQ)\) acts on the values
+of \(\chi\) by \(\chi(g)\mapsto\chi(g)^u\) for some odd \(u\), and therefore
+sends \(P_{\chi,\tau}\) to \(P_{\chi^u,\tau}\).  Condition
+\eqref{eq:odd-adams-determinant-invariance} fixes this polynomial under the
+whole Galois group.  Its coefficients are rational algebraic integers, hence
+integers.  The same argument applies to \(\tau'\).
+
+For the collapse, the abelian specialization of
+\eqref{eq:fixed-determinant-open-disc} gives the absolutely convergent identity
+\begin{align}
+ \Delta_\chi(z)
+ &=-\sum_{r,m\ge1}\frac{\mu(m)}{rm}
+      \Log_0H_{\chi^m}(z^{rm})\notag\\
+ &=-\sum_{k\ge1}\frac1k\sum_{m\mid k}\mu(m)
+      \Log_0H_{\chi^m}(z^k).
+ \label{eq:odd-adams-collapse-before-divisors}
+\end{align}
+Write \(k=2^jq\), where \(q\) is odd.  The odd divisors contributing to the
+inner sum have the form \(m=d\), \(d\mid q\), and
+\[
+ \sum_{\substack{m\mid k\\m\ {\rm odd}}}\mu(m)
+ =\sum_{d\mid q}\mu(d)
+ =\begin{cases}1,&q=1,\\0,&q>1.\end{cases}
+\]
+If \(j\ge1\), the square-free even divisors are exactly \(m=2d\), with
+\(d\mid q\) odd, and
+\[
+ \sum_{\substack{m\mid k\\m\ {\rm even}}}\mu(m)
+ =\sum_{d\mid q}\mu(2d)
+ =-\sum_{d\mid q}\mu(d).
+\]
+For odd \(d\), condition (OA) gives
+\[
+ H_{\chi^d}=H_\chi,\qquad
+ H_{\chi^{2d}}=H_{(\chi^2)^d}=H_{\chi^2}.
+\]
+Thus the inner divisor sum in
+\eqref{eq:odd-adams-collapse-before-divisors} vanishes unless \(q=1\);
+for \(k=1\) it is \(\Log_0H_\chi(z)\), and for \(k=2^j\), \(j\ge1\), it is
+\[
+ \Log_0H_\chi(z^{2^j})-\Log_0H_{\chi^2}(z^{2^j}).
+\]
+Substitution proves \eqref{eq:odd-adams-mobius-collapse}.  This is an
+identity of analytic germs, and hence throughout the common Perron disk.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{theorem}[Odd-Adams-invariant finite radial determination]
+\label{thm:odd-adams-abelian-two-group-finite-sampling}
+Let \(G\) be a finite abelian \(2\)-group.  Let
+\(\tau:E(\Gamma)\to G\) and \(\tau':E(\Gamma')\to G\) be one-step
+cocycles over primitive non-negative integral base matrices \(A,A'\), whose
+sizes are at most \(V\) and whose Perron roots are
+\(\lambda,\lambda'>1\).  Assume that both cocycles satisfy (OA) in
+\eqref{eq:odd-adams-determinant-invariance}.  Put
+\[
+ x=\min\{\lambda^{-1},(\lambda')^{-1}\},\qquad
+ M(V)=2V\lceil\log_2(4V)\rceil.
+\]
+For \(g\in G\), define
+\[
+ \mathcal E_g^\tau(y)
+ =\sum_{n\ge1}p_{n,g}(\tau)\log(1-y^n),\qquad 0<y<x,
+\]
+and define \(\mathcal E_g^{\tau'}\) analogously.  Suppose that
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-adams-sampled-profile-equality}
+ \mathcal E_g^\tau(y_i)=\mathcal E_g^{\tau'}(y_i)
+ \qquad(g\in G,\ 1\le i\le M(V))
+\end{equation}
+at \(M(V)\) distinct radii in \((0,x)\), at least one of which is algebraic.
+Then
+\[
+ p_{n,g}(\tau)=p_{n,g}(\tau')
+ \qquad(n\ge1,\ g\in G).
+\]
+The number \(M(V)\) of radial locations is independent of the rank and
+exponent of \(G\), while the total number of scalar equalities in
+\eqref{eq:odd-adams-sampled-profile-equality} is \(\abs G M(V)\).
+Neither a common base nor a strict twisted spectral gap is required.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+All profile series converge absolutely on the stated interval by the
+periodic-point estimate in \Cref{thm:finite-radial-sampling}.  Summing
+\eqref{eq:odd-adams-sampled-profile-equality} over \(g\) gives
+\[
+ \log\det(I-y_iA)=\log\det(I-y_iA')
+ \qquad(1\le i\le M(V)).
+\]
+The determinants are positive on \((0,x)\).  Their difference has degree at
+most \(V\), vanishes at the sampled radii and at zero, and hence is zero:
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-adams-base-determinant-equality}
+ P_{\mathbf1,\tau}(z)=\det(I-zA)=\det(I-zA')
+ =P_{\mathbf1,\tau'}(z).
+\end{equation}
+Thus \(H_{\mathbf1}=1\).
+
+Fourier transformation of the sampled element-profile equalities gives
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-adams-sampled-fourier-equality}
+ \Delta_\chi(y_i)
+ =-\sum_{g\in G}\chi(g)
+   \bigl(\mathcal E_g^\tau(y_i)-\mathcal E_g^{\tau'}(y_i)\bigr)
+ =0
+\end{equation}
+for every \(\chi\in\widehat G\) and every \(i\).  We prove
+\(H_\chi=1\) by induction on the order of \(\chi\).  The order-one case is
+\eqref{eq:odd-adams-base-determinant-equality}.  Assume the assertion for
+all characters of order less than \(2^a\), and let \(\chi\) have order
+\(2^a\).  Then \(H_{\chi^2}=1\), so
+\Cref{lem:odd-adams-mobius-collapse} reduces to
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-adams-inductive-dyadic-orbit}
+ \Delta_\chi(y)
+ =-\sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}\log H_\chi(y^{2^j})
+ \qquad(0<y<x).
+\end{equation}
+
+By \Cref{lem:odd-adams-mobius-collapse}, \(H_\chi\in\QQ(z)^\times\).
+Entrywise,
+\[
+ \abs{(A_{\chi,\tau})_{uv}}\le A_{uv},\qquad
+ \abs{(A_{\chi,\tau'})_{uv}}\le A'_{uv}.
+\]
+Perron-weighted domination therefore makes both character determinants
+zero-free on their open Perron disks.  Since they are real polynomials with
+value one at zero, they and \(H_\chi\) are positive on \((0,x)\).
+
+Choose an algebraic sampled radius \(y_0\).  Equations
+\eqref{eq:odd-adams-sampled-fourier-equality} and
+\eqref{eq:odd-adams-inductive-dyadic-orbit} give
+\[
+ \prod_{j\ge0}H_\chi(y_0^{2^j})^{2^{-j}}=1.
+\]
+If \(H_\chi\ne1\), \Cref{thm:general-rational-p-mahler-lifting} with \(p=2\)
+gives the unique normalized \(R_\chi\in\QQ(z)^\times\) such that
+\[
+ H_\chi(z)=\frac{R_\chi(z^2)}{R_\chi(z)^2},\qquad R_\chi(y_0)=1.
+\]
+Write \(H_\chi=P_{0,\chi}/P_{1,\chi}\) in reduced form and put
+\(D_\chi=\deg P_{0,\chi}+\deg P_{1,\chi}\).  Both determinants have degree
+at most \(V\), so \(D_\chi\le2V\).  The rational telescope and
+\Cref{prop:logarithmic-mahler-divisor-bound} show that every real zero of
+\(\Delta_\chi\) is a non-zero root of \(R_\chi-1\), and that there are at
+most
+\[
+ b_2(D_\chi)-1
+ =D_\chi\lceil\log_2(2D_\chi)\rceil-1
+ \le M(V)-1
+\]
+such roots.  This contradicts the \(M(V)\) distinct zeros in
+\eqref{eq:odd-adams-sampled-fourier-equality}.  Hence \(H_\chi=1\), closing
+the induction.
+
+All character determinants now agree between the two systems.  The
+cross-base periodic-data dictionary in \Cref{prop:comparison-dictionary},
+followed by Fourier inversion on \(G\), recovers every
+\(p_{n,g}\), as asserted.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{remark}[Concrete scope of (OA)]
+\label{rem:odd-adams-concrete-scope}
+Condition (OA) is automatic for \(G=(C_2)^r\).  A stronger entrywise
+sufficient condition for a general abelian \(2\)-group is that, for every
+ordered vertex pair, every \(g\in G\), and every odd \(u\), the number of
+\(g\)-labelled edges equals the number of \(g^u\)-labelled edges.  It then
+gives \(A_{\chi^u}=A_\chi\), not merely equality of their determinants.
+
+For \(C_4=\langle a\rangle\), this condition says exactly that the
+\(a\)- and \(a^{-1}\)-labelled edge counts agree entrywise; the \(e\)- and
+\(a^2\)-counts are unrestricted.  It does not force factorization through
+\(C_2\): a one-vertex graph with equally many \(a\)- and \(a^{-1}\)-loops
+has primitive base and holonomy subgroup \(C_4\).  Likewise, assigning equal
+counts on each odd-power orbit in \(C_{2^s}\) gives examples with genuine
+holonomy of order \(2^s\).
+\end{remark}

+\subsection{Realizable collision and certificate lower bounds}
+\label{sec:realizable-collision-lower-bounds}
+
+We begin with a relative realization fact for sign determinants.  It is
+sufficient for both the explicit collision family and the abstract
+certificate-degree family.
+
+\begin{lemma}[Relative sign-determinant realization]
+\label{lem:relative-sign-determinant-realization}
+Let \(P_0,P_1\in\ZZ[z]\) satisfy
+\[
+ P_0(0)=P_1(0)=1,\qquad P_0\equiv P_1\pmod2.
+\]
+Put \(d=\max\{1,\deg P_0,\deg P_1\}\).  There are a positive integral
+\(d\times d\) matrix \(A\) and two one-step \(C_2\)-cocycles on the same
+marked base graph with sign blocks \(C_0,C_1\) such that
+\[
+ \det(I-zC_i)=P_i(z)\qquad(i=0,1),
+\]
+and both sign blocks have strict twisted spectral gap:
+\[
+ \rad(C_i)<\rad(A)\qquad(i=0,1).
+\]
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Pad both polynomials to degree \(d\), and let \(C_i\) be the integral
+companion matrix of the monic polynomial
+\[
+ t^dP_i(t^{-1}).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ \det(I-zC_i)=z^d\det(z^{-1}I-C_i)=P_i(z).
+\]
+The congruence of the polynomials makes the two standard companion matrices
+entrywise congruent modulo two.  For each entry choose a positive integer
+\(A_{jk}\), in this common parity class, with
+\[
+ A_{jk}>\max\{\abs{(C_0)_{jk}},\abs{(C_1)_{jk}}\}.
+\]
+Thus \(A\) is positive and hence primitive.  For each \(i\), the non-negative
+integral matrices
+\[
+ \frac{A+C_i}{2},\qquad \frac{A-C_i}{2}
+\]
+count respectively the \(e\)- and \(s\)-labelled edges of a \(C_2\)-cocycle
+on this same marked base.  Finally,
+\[
+ \rad(C_i)\le\rad(\abs{C_i})<\rad(A)
+\]
+by strict Perron--Frobenius monotonicity, proving the gap.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{theorem}[Realizable linear multi-collisions]
+\label{thm:realizable-linear-multicollisions}
+For every integer \(m\ge1\), there is a positive primitive directed
+multigraph with
+\[
+ v_m=4m+2
+\]
+vertices and two one-step \(C_2\)-cocycles \(\tau_m,\tau_m'\) on the same
+marked base, both with strict twisted spectral gap, for which the primitive
+length--element data differ but
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:realizable-linear-profile-collisions}
+ \mathcal E_e^{\tau_m}(y_{m,i})
+ =\mathcal E_e^{\tau_m'}(y_{m,i}),\qquad
+ \mathcal E_s^{\tau_m}(y_{m,i})
+ =\mathcal E_s^{\tau_m'}(y_{m,i})
+ \quad(1\le i\le m)
+\end{equation}
+at \(m\) distinct rational radii in the open Perron interval.
+
+More explicitly, put
+\[
+ s_i=64(m+1)+4i\qquad(1\le i\le m)
+\]
+and let \(C_m\) be the \((2m+1)\times(2m+1)\) integral matrix indexed by
+\[
+ u_0,\ldots,u_m,w_1,\ldots,w_m
+\]
+whose only non-zero entries are
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:realizable-collision-Cm-entries}
+ \begin{aligned}
+  (C_m)_{u_{i-1},u_i}&=-4,&
+  (C_m)_{u_{i-1},w_i}&=s_i &&(1\le i\le m),\\
+  (C_m)_{w_i,u_i}&=s_i,&
+  (C_m)_{u_m,u_0}&=-4.
+ \end{aligned}
+\end{equation}
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:realizable-collision-Qm}
+ Q_m(z):=\det(I-zC_m)
+ =1+4z\prod_{i=1}^m(-4z+s_i^2z^2).
+\end{equation}
+Writing \(n=2m+1\), take the two \(2n\times2n\) sign blocks
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:realizable-collision-sign-blocks}
+ B_m=\begin{pmatrix}0&C_m/2\\2I_n&0\end{pmatrix},
+ \qquad B_m'=C_m\oplus C_m.
+\end{equation}
+They satisfy
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:realizable-collision-determinants}
+ \det(I-zB_m)=Q_m(z^2),\qquad
+ \det(I-zB_m')=Q_m(z)^2.
+\end{equation}
+The common base may be chosen as
+\[
+ A_m=s_mJ_{4m+2},\qquad
+ \lambda_m=s_m(4m+2),
+\]
+and the collision radii are
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:realizable-collision-radii}
+ y_{m,i}=\frac4{s_i^2}\qquad(1\le i\le m).
+\end{equation}
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+In the directed support of \(C_m\), every non-trivial cycle must traverse
+from \(u_0\) through the stages \(1,\ldots,m\) and then use the closing edge
+\(u_m\to u_0\).  At stage \(i\), it uses either the direct edge of weight
+\(-4\), contributing \(-4z\), or the two-edge detour through \(w_i\),
+contributing \(s_i^2z^2\).  A single directed cycle contributes the negative
+of the product of its weighted \(z\)-edges to \(\det(I-zC_m)\).  The closing
+edge contributes \(-4z\), so summing the \(2^m\) choices gives
+\[
+ 1-(-4z)\prod_{i=1}^m(-4z+s_i^2z^2),
+\]
+which is \eqref{eq:realizable-collision-Qm}.
+
+All entries of \(C_m\) are divisible by four.  Hence the blocks in
+\eqref{eq:realizable-collision-sign-blocks} are integral and even.  The
+standard block determinant identity gives
+\[
+ \det(I-zB_m)=\det(I-z^2C_m)=Q_m(z^2),
+\]
+while the direct sum gives the second identity in
+\eqref{eq:realizable-collision-determinants}.  Moreover
+\(\abs{B_m},\abs{B_m'}\le A_m\) entrywise and both inequalities are strict
+somewhere.  Since \(A_m\) is positive, the matrices
+\((A_m\pm B_m)/2\) and \((A_m\pm B_m')/2\) realize two cocycles on the same
+marked base, and strict Perron--Frobenius monotonicity gives
+\[
+ \rad(B_m),\rad(B_m')<\rad(A_m)=\lambda_m.
+\]
+
+The \(s_i\) are strictly increasing, so the radii in
+\eqref{eq:realizable-collision-radii} are positive, rational, and distinct.
+The largest is \(4/s_1^2\), and direct expansion gives
+\[
+ s_1^2-4s_m(4m+2)
+ =3008m^2+7136m+4112>0.
+\]
+Thus every \(y_{m,i}<\lambda_m^{-1}\).  The \(i\)-th factor in
+\eqref{eq:realizable-collision-Qm} vanishes at \(y_{m,i}\), so
+\[
+ Q_m(y_{m,i})=1.
+\]
+
+For the sign-determinant ratio in the orientation of
+\Cref{prop:c2-standard-zeta-ratio}, put
+\[
+ H_m(z)=\frac{\det(I-zB_m)}{\det(I-zB_m')}
+ =\frac{Q_m(z^2)}{Q_m(z)^2}.
+\]
+The dyadic identity \eqref{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity} and the
+rational telescope give
+\[
+ F_\varepsilon^{\tau_m}(y)-F_\varepsilon^{\tau_m'}(y)
+ =2\log Q_m(y).
+\]
+It vanishes at every \(y_{m,i}\).  The trivial blocks are both \(A_m\), so
+Fourier inversion for \(C_2\) proves both equalities in
+\eqref{eq:realizable-linear-profile-collisions}.
+
+The polynomial \(Q_m\) is non-constant.  If
+\(Q_m(z^2)=Q_m(z)^2\), comparison of the least non-constant term would give
+two different degrees; hence \(H_m\ne1\).  The comparison dictionary therefore
+shows that the two primitive length--element data sets differ.  Finally,
+\[
+ H_m(z)=
+ \frac{\zeta_{\widetilde X_{\tau_m'}}(z)}
+      {\zeta_{\widetilde X_{\tau_m}}(z)}
+\]
+by \Cref{prop:c2-standard-zeta-ratio}, so these are collisions of standard
+Artin--Mazur zeta ratios.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Linear lower bound for radial determination]
+\label{cor:linear-radial-sampling-lower-bound}
+Let \(\mathsf N_{C_2}(V)\) be the least integer \(N\) such that, for every
+pair of one-step \(C_2\)-cocycles over primitive bases of at most \(V\)
+vertices, equality of both element profiles at \(N\) distinct radii in the
+common open Perron interval, with at least one algebraic radius, forces
+equality of all primitive length--element data.  Then, for \(V\ge6\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:linear-radial-sampling-lower-bound}
+ \mathsf N_{C_2}(V)\ge
+ \left\lfloor\frac{V-2}{4}\right\rfloor+1.
+\end{equation}
+In particular, the worst-case radial sampling complexity is
+\(\Omega(V)\), so the \(O(V\log V)\) upper bound cannot be replaced by
+\(o(V)\).
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Take \(m=\lfloor(V-2)/4\rfloor\), which is positive for \(V\ge6\).
+Then \(4m+2\le V\), and
+\Cref{thm:realizable-linear-multicollisions} gives two distinct periodic-data
+sets agreeing at \(m\) rational radii.  A universal determination number must
+therefore be at least \(m+1\).
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Realizable logarithmic certificate-degree sharpness]
+\label{cor:realizable-logarithmic-certificate-sharpness}
+There is a sequence of pairs of strict-gap \(C_2\)-cocycles on common
+primitive \(V_J\)-vertex bases whose standard Artin--Mazur zeta ratios have
+unique normalized rational Mahler certificates of degree
+\[
+ \frac{V_J}{2}\log_2V_J=\Omega(V_J\log V_J).
+\]
+Thus the \(O(D\log D)\) certificate-degree bound has the correct order even
+on realizable standard \(C_2\)-cover zeta ratios.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Let \(Q(z)=1-2z\), \(J\ge0\), and
+\[
+ R_J(z)=\prod_{j=0}^JQ(z^{2^j})^{2^{J-j}}.
+\]
+As in \Cref{rem:logarithmic-mahler-degree-sharpness},
+\[
+ H_J(z):=\frac{R_J(z^2)}{R_J(z)^2}
+ =\frac{Q(z^{2^{J+1}})}{Q(z)^{2^{J+1}}},
+ \qquad
+ \deg R_J=(J+1)2^J.
+\]
+Put \(V_J=2^{J+1}\).  The numerator and denominator of \(H_J\) have degree
+\(V_J\), constant term one, and are both congruent to one modulo two.
+\Cref{lem:relative-sign-determinant-realization} therefore realizes them as
+the two sign determinants of strict-gap cocycles on one positive
+\(V_J\)-vertex base.  Their ratio is the corresponding standard zeta ratio.
+Normalized injectivity of the Mahler coboundary map makes \(R_J\) its unique
+certificate, and
+\[
+ \deg R_J=(J+1)2^J=\frac{V_J}{2}\log_2V_J.
+\]
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{remark}[Three distinct notions of sharpness]
+\label{rem:three-sharpness-levels}
+\Cref{cor:realizable-logarithmic-certificate-sharpness} concerns certificate
+degree and upgrades the abstract divisor family to standard realizable zeta
+ratios.  It does not produce \(\Omega(V\log V)\) positive real collisions.
+The genuine sampling statement is
+\Cref{cor:linear-radial-sampling-lower-bound}, which gives \(\Omega(V)\)
+distinct rational collisions.  No matching \(\Omega(V\log V)\) positive-real
+sampling lower bound is claimed.
+\end{remark}

+def rational_critical_denominator_audit(order: int = 12) -> dict[str, object]:
+    """Check the (p q)^(2n-1) denominator bound for rational p-products."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    p_zero = 1 + z / 2 + z**2 / 3
+    p_one = 1 - z / 5
+    denominators = [
+        int(sp.denom(coefficient))
+        for polynomial in (p_zero, p_one)
+        for coefficient in sp.Poly(polynomial, z).all_coeffs()
+    ]
+    q = 1
+    for denominator in denominators:
+        q = sp.ilcm(q, denominator)
+
+    all_bounds_hold = True
+    nonintegral_coefficient_seen = False
+    radices = (2, 3, 4, 5)
+    for radix in radices:
+        coefficients = [sp.Integer(1)]
+        for degree in range(1, order + 1):
+            unknown = sp.Symbol(f"f_{degree}")
+            truncated = sum(
+                coefficient * z**index
+                for index, coefficient in enumerate(coefficients)
+            ) + unknown * z**degree
+            coefficient_equation = sp.expand(
+                p_one * truncated**radix
+                - p_zero * truncated.subs(z, z**radix)
+            ).coeff(z, degree)
+            linear_coefficient = coefficient_equation.coeff(unknown)
+            value = sp.cancel(
+                -coefficient_equation.subs(unknown, 0) / linear_coefficient
+            )
+            coefficients.append(value)
+            scaled = sp.cancel((radix * q) ** (2 * degree - 1) * value)
+            all_bounds_hold &= bool(scaled.is_Integer)
+            nonintegral_coefficient_seen |= not bool(value.is_Integer)
+
+        truncated = sum(
+            coefficient * z**index
+            for index, coefficient in enumerate(coefficients)
+        )
+        residual = sp.series(
+            p_one * truncated**radix
+            - p_zero * truncated.subs(z, z**radix),
+            z,
+            0,
+            order + 1,
+        ).removeO()
+        all_bounds_hold &= sp.expand(residual) == 0
+
+    return {
+        "radices": radices,
+        "order": order,
+        "clearing_denominator": q,
+        "all_bounds_hold": all_bounds_hold,
+        "nonintegral_coefficient_seen": nonintegral_coefficient_seen,
+    }

+def realizable_multicollision_family_audit(max_m: int = 4) -> dict[str, object]:
+    """Check the parametric standard-cover collision identities exactly."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    vertex_counts: list[int] = []
+    collision_counts: list[int] = []
+    determinant_identities_hold = True
+    all_radii_in_perron_interval = True
+    same_base_realization_holds = True
+    strict_gap_certified = True
+
+    for m in range(1, max_m + 1):
+        n = 2 * m + 1
+        size = 2 * n
+        scales = [64 * (m + 1) + 4 * index for index in range(1, m + 1)]
+        c_matrix = sp.zeros(n)
+        for index, scale in enumerate(scales, 1):
+            c_matrix[index - 1, index] = -4
+            c_matrix[index - 1, m + index] = scale
+            c_matrix[m + index, index] = scale
+        c_matrix[m, 0] = -4
+
+        q_polynomial = sp.expand((sp.eye(n) - z * c_matrix).det())
+        expected_q = sp.expand(
+            1 + 4 * z * sp.prod(-4 * z + scale**2 * z**2 for scale in scales)
+        )
+        first_block = sp.zeros(size)
+        first_block[:n, n:] = c_matrix / 2
+        first_block[n:, :n] = 2 * sp.eye(n)
+        second_block = sp.diag(c_matrix, c_matrix)
+        first_determinant = sp.expand((sp.eye(size) - z * first_block).det())
+        second_determinant = sp.expand((sp.eye(size) - z * second_block).det())
+        determinant_identities_hold &= all(
+            (
+                q_polynomial == expected_q,
+                first_determinant == sp.expand(q_polynomial.subs(z, z**2)),
+                second_determinant == sp.expand(q_polynomial**2),
+            )
+        )
+
+        base_entry = scales[-1]
+        base = sp.ones(size) * base_entry
+        compatibility = all(
+            bool(
+                block[row, column].is_Integer
+                and (base[row, column] - block[row, column]) % 2 == 0
+                and abs(block[row, column]) <= base[row, column]
+            )
+            for block in (first_block, second_block)
+            for row in range(size)
+            for column in range(size)
+        )
+        same_base_realization_holds &= compatibility
+        strict_gap_certified &= all(
+            any(
+                abs(block[row, column]) < base[row, column]
+                for row in range(size)
+                for column in range(size)
+            )
+            for block in (first_block, second_block)
+        )
+
+        radii = tuple(sp.Rational(4, scale**2) for scale in scales)
+        perron_root = base_entry * size
+        all_radii_in_perron_interval &= all(
+            0 < radius < sp.Rational(1, perron_root) for radius in radii
+        )
+        collisions = tuple(
+            radius for radius in radii if q_polynomial.subs(z, radius) == 1
+        )
+        vertex_counts.append(size)
+        collision_counts.append(len(collisions))
+
+    return {
+        "vertex_counts": tuple(vertex_counts),
+        "collision_counts": tuple(collision_counts),
+        "determinant_identities_hold": determinant_identities_hold,
+        "all_radii_in_perron_interval": all_radii_in_perron_interval,
+        "same_base_realization_holds": same_base_realization_holds,
+        "strict_gap_certified": strict_gap_certified,
+    }

+def _integral_companion_for_reciprocal(polynomial: sp.Expr) -> sp.Matrix:
+    """Return C with det(I-zC)=polynomial for a normalized integral input."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    poly = sp.Poly(polynomial, z)
+    degree = max(1, poly.degree())
+    coefficients = [sp.Integer(poly.nth(index)) for index in range(degree + 1)]
+    companion = sp.zeros(degree)
+    for row in range(1, degree):
+        companion[row, row - 1] = 1
+    for row in range(degree):
+        companion[row, degree - 1] = -coefficients[degree - row]
+    return companion
+
